identity.title: Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: Enable large language models to self-correct effectively.

gap.claim: Existing self-correction training methods typically require multiple models, a stronger model, or additional supervision.

contributions.claim: SCoRe, a multi-turn online reinforcement-learning approach that trains self-correction using entirely self-generated data.
A training design combining on-policy correction traces, regularization, a base-model RL initialization, and a reward bonus for amplifying self-correction.
The authors report improved self-correction on Gemini 1.0 Pro and 1.5 Flash.

stated_novelty.claim: The proposed approach addresses prior supervision and model-dependence shortcomings through multi-turn online RL with entirely self-generated data.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that supervised fine-tuning on offline model-generated correction traces is insufficient, due either to distribution mismatch or preference for correction modes that are ineffective at test time.
The authors report state-of-the-art self-correction performance for Gemini 1.0 Pro and 1.5 Flash, with base-model improvements of 15.6% and 9.1% respectively on MATH and HumanEval.

narrative_sequence.summary: Self-correction is desirable but reported as largely ineffective in modern LLMs.
Existing training approaches rely on extra models or supervision; offline-trace SFT is reported as insufficient.
SCoRe trains on the model’s own correction-trace distribution and regularizes learning toward test-time-effective strategies.
Its regularization uses initial RL to reduce collapse susceptibility and a reward bonus to amplify self-correction.
The authors report gains on Gemini models across MATH and HumanEval.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links offline SFT failure to distribution mismatch and mode preference, then describes on-policy training and regularization as responses.

lessons.interpretation: A method claim is more informative when its design choices are explicitly tied to diagnosed failure modes.
lessons.application: Frame each proposed component as addressing a specific training or evaluation mismatch, and state the intended effect.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the mechanism-to-failure link has not been established or the method has no identifiable failure mode.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact evaluation metric, comparison baselines, statistical uncertainty, or whether the reported percentages are relative or absolute improvements.
Details of the RL reward, regularization strength, tasks, and ablations are not provided.
